pages.text: HF radios are made for one band each: $(thing)80 m$(), $(thing)40 m$(), $(thing)20 m$() or $(thing)10 m$(). They reach far beyond the horizon by $(l:radiocraft:propagation/bands)skip$(/l).$(li)$(thing)SSB$(): voice. 40 and 80 m use lower sideband, 20 and 10 m upper.$(li)$(thing)CW$(): Morse code, sent with the key on the radio's screen. CW gets through where voice cannot.

Turn it on with the power switch, pick a mode, tune with the big knob (1 kHz a step) and hold $(thing)PTT$() to talk. The screen on the model shows the frequency, mode and S-meter. A comparator next to it reads the S-meter too.$(br2)An HF radio draws 8 FE/t listening and 26 transmitting.

pages.name: A 20 m station
pages.text: Radio, coax, a 1:1 balun and two poles. String antenna wire from the balun to each pole: 5 blocks each way on 20 m. See $(l:radiocraft:antennas/dipole)Dipole$(/l).
